Question:
The figure below shows a polygon \(ABCDEFGH,\) consisting of rectangles and right triangles. When cut out and folded on the dotted lines, the polygon forms a triangular prism. Suppose that:

\[ AH = EF = 8 \]

and

\[ GH = 14. \]

What is the volume of the prism?

[Figure 1](figures/2022_AMC_8_Q24_question_fig1.svg)
Solution:
Use \(\triangle BJG\) as one triangular end of the prism. The net shows that \(AHJB\) is a rectangle, so \(BJ=AH=8\). It also shows that \(EFID\) is a rectangle, so \(DI=EF=8\).

When folded, the rectangular side faces all span the same distance between the two triangular ends. Thus \(HJ=DI=8\); that is the prism's length. Since \(H,J,G\) lie on one straight side of the net,

\[
JG=HG-HJ=14-8=6.
\]

The marked right angle is at \(J\), so the triangular end has perpendicular legs \(BJ=8\) and \(JG=6\). Its area is \(\frac12\cdot8\cdot6=24\).

The folded view helps track which edges become the prism's length:

[Figure 2](figures/2022_AMC_8_Q24_solution_official_prism.png)

Multiplying base area by prism length gives

\[
V=24\cdot8=\boxed{192},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). Keeping the triangular end separate from the prism's length is the key to reading the net.
